claims.explanation: Deforolimus is an allosteric mTORC1 inhibitor (rapalog), so sensitivity is expected in tumors whose growth depends on mTORC1-driven translation downstream of activated PI3K/AKT signaling. The most consistent genomic correlate in the sensitive lines is loss-of-function of PTEN (and, more broadly, PI3K pathway activation via PIK3CA mutation or PTEN loss), which relieves negative regulation of AKT/mTORC1 and creates dependence on mTORC1; lines without such lesions (e.g., RAS/BRAF-only melanomas, FBXW7-mutant colorectal/gastric lines) are relatively resistant.

features.basis: PTEN loss activates PI3K/AKT/mTORC1; enriched in sensitive lines (ZR751, 786O, HEC265, KALS1)
Activating PI3K mutation drives mTORC1 dependence; seen in HGC27, KYSE510, SNU840
Higher mTOR pathway activity/target engagement predicts rapalog response
AKT overexpression activates mTORC1 and is reported in mTOR-pathway-deregulated tumors
S6K1 overexpression marks mTORC1-driven tumors sensitive to rapalogs
4EBP1 overexpression reflects mTORC1-dependent translation
eIF4E overexpression reported with mTOR pathway deregulation
LKB1 loss may relieve AMPK restraint on mTORC1; seen in SNU840, KALS1
NF1 loss activates RAS/MAPK and can co-activate mTOR; seen in KALS1, S117, BICR6
RAS-driven lines (GSU, T3M4, CL11, SNU410) are relatively resistant, suggesting MAPK bypass
BRAF-mutant melanomas (UACC62, IGR37) are among least affected
FBXW7-mutant lines (NCIH1648, CL11, MKN1, SNUC5) cluster in resistant group
